summary.intent: Recover uncommitted Phase 37 (parallel batch upload pipeline) roadmap work from a previous session, gather implementation context via structured discussion, and produce a research-backed plan for the phase.
summary.outcome: Phase 37 CONTEXT.md and DISCUSSION-LOG.md were created and committed with locked decisions on concurrency model, SDK API shape, Web Worker encryption, error handling, and desktop scope. Research (37-RESEARCH.md) and a validation strategy (37-VALIDATION.md) were also produced and committed.

repo: Phase 37 planning artifacts were created locally in a prior session but never committed or pushed — only the phase directory shell and ROADMAP.md edits existed as unstaged/untracked changes.

The upload pipeline is sequential by design: useDropUpload.ts loops files one-by-one, each calling client.uploadFile() which does encrypt → IPFS pin → add FilePointer → publish folder IPNS — resulting in N IPNS publishes for N files.

withOperation() in the SDK serializes all SDK operations, meaning naive concurrent calls to uploadFile() would just queue and remain sequential — Option C (concurrency at web layer with existing API) is not viable.

The desktop FUSE layer receives files one-at-a-time via release() callbacks and has no batch context, so a Rust upload_files() batch method would not naturally be used by FUSE without a separate write-coalescing layer.

The stale-children race window in batch uploads (another device publishes new children during a long encrypt+pin operation) is a known foot gun — mitigation is re-reading folder metadata just before the final publish and merging children.
Per-file progress, cancel, retry, and error states were already wired in Phase 36 via the Zustand upload store, providing a foundation for Phase 37 UI changes.

code.finding: Sequential file upload loop — each iteration calls client.uploadFile() triggering a full encrypt+pin+publish cycle per file.
uploadFile() performs encrypt+pin+publish as one atomic unit, making it impossible to batch the folder update with the current API.
FUSE release() callback triggers per-file upload — no batch context available at this layer.
Rust SDK uses a queue for upload operations; write-coalescing for batch desktop uploads would require changes here.

workflow: The GSD discuss-phase workflow routes to assumptions mode vs discuss mode via a config flag (workflow.discuss_mode) — assumptions mode spawns a codebase analyzer agent to surface decisions proactively rather than asking interview-style questions.
Deferred ideas are captured explicitly in CONTEXT.md to prevent loss without expanding scope — adaptive concurrency, FUSE write-coalescing, and accumulated retry batching were all noted this way.
The plan-phase workflow gates on whether research exists before spawning the planner, and generates a VALIDATION.md as a separate artifact alongside RESEARCH.md and PLAN.md files.
